# `check_photometry`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the photometry check view stage.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc7db0, StartViewStarStage @0x3c1570 (64-bit build); camera library ASI_CAM_SetControlValue @0x38dc0, SetExposure @0x38680 (control 1 exposure conversion); firmware 9.75 request members from the 9.75 reports |

Starts ViewStar stage 5 with no stage parameters: stops any existing view, changes view mode, clears the subframe, selects page 0 (and may change the view size on some wide or model branches) and starts the named View worker asynchronously. Success acknowledges the start. The worker sets camera exposure control 1 to 2000000 (READ), that is 2 s in microseconds (unit INFERRED from the camera library's conversion of the value to sensor lines), then captures, solves the frame and validates the target pixel position; its failures (exposure failed, solve failed, out of image, aborted, conversion error) are asynchronous function status, not RPC codes. The CheckPhotoMetry event can carry a completion coordinate pair (ra_dec_deg_j2000, RA and Dec in degrees, J2000 INFERRED) in its completed state; the binding to the exact event envelope is not established here. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: optional params magV (default 13.0) and offsetDeg (default 2.5, degrees INFERRED) select the reference-star magnitude limit and search offset; the worker may download reference stars when the internet is reachable. The download is an outbound HTTP(S) request to a vendor catalogue service (address not recorded; unresolved), and the CheckPhotoMetry event gains has_download_ref_star at complete. Firmware 9.31: params not read.

Side effects: Interrupts existing imaging: stops the current view, changes view mode and page, then starts an asynchronous worker that changes exposure control and captures. Open camera required. No request timeout. Every full call also makes the shared diagnostic log writes.

Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"check_photometry"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Firmware 9.31: not read. Firmware 9.75: optional object; a non-object gives 107. [READ] |
| `params.magV` | number | no | - | Magnitude limit, default 13.0. Not a number gives 102. [READ] |
| `params.offsetDeg` | number | no | - | Offset, default 2.5 (degrees INFERRED from the name). Not a number gives 102; 0 or less gives 204. [READ; unit INFERRED] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 318 | Camera not opened | `device not connected` |
| 102 | Firmware 9.75: magV or offsetDeg is not a number | `invalid argument` |
| 204 | Firmware 9.75: offsetDeg is 0 or less | `out of range` |
| 107 | Firmware 9.75: params is not an object | `expected object` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Starting the same stage while it is already running returns success early. Other worker-start, stop and page failures forward the thread-local code and are not enumerated.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":91,"method":"check_photometry"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"check_photometry","result":0,"code":0,"id":91}
```

Reply, camera-closed:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"check_photometry","error":"device not connected","code":318,"id":92}
```
